config.title: Chicago Field Guide
config.subtitle: Measured from Union Station, where the Amtrak from Champaign arrives
config.guideIntro: One guide per part of the city, each a good day on foot and by L or bus. Distances are straight-line from Union Station.

sites.name: Art Institute of Chicago
sites.desc: One of the world's great encyclopedic museums, in an 1893 Beaux-Arts building with Renzo Piano's Modern Wing.

sites.name: Chicago Cultural Center
sites.desc: The 1897 former public library, with the largest Tiffany glass dome in the world. Free.

sites.name: Millennium Park and Cloud Gate
sites.desc: Anish Kapoor's Cloud Gate, Jaume Plensa's Crown Fountain and Frank Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion.

sites.name: Lurie Garden
sites.desc: A perennial meadow garden in Millennium Park designed by Piet Oudolf with Gustafson Guthrie Nichol.

sites.name: Buckingham Fountain
sites.desc: The 1927 Beaux-Arts fountain in Grant Park, with water shows in season.

sites.name: The Rookery
sites.desc: Burnham and Root's 1888 office building, with a light court remodeled by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1905.

sites.name: Monadnock Building
sites.desc: Burnham and Root's north half (1891) is among the tallest load-bearing masonry buildings ever built.

sites.name: Marquette Building
sites.desc: Holabird and Roche's 1895 Chicago School office building with a Tiffany mosaic lobby.

sites.name: Reliance Building
sites.desc: An 1895 glass and terra cotta tower that anticipated the modern curtain wall. Now a hotel.

sites.name: Sullivan Center
sites.desc: Louis Sullivan's former Carson Pirie Scott store, with cast iron ornament over the corner entrance.

sites.name: Auditorium Building
sites.desc: Adler and Sullivan's 1889 opera house, hotel and office block with a gold-leaf theater. Tours offered.

sites.name: Chicago Board of Trade Building
sites.desc: The 1930 Art Deco tower capped by a statue of Ceres, closing the view down LaSalle Street.

sites.name: Chicago Federal Center
sites.desc: Mies van der Rohe's black steel federal plaza, set off by Alexander Calder's red Flamingo.

sites.name: Inland Steel Building
sites.desc: SOM's 1958 stainless steel tower with its columns on the outside, a Chicago modernist landmark.

sites.name: Harold Washington Library Center
sites.desc: The 1991 central library with green owl acroteria and a skylit winter garden.

sites.name: Willis Tower Skydeck
sites.desc: SOM's 1973 bundled-tube skyscraper, with glass ledges 103 floors up.

sites.name: Chicago Theatre
sites.desc: The 1921 movie palace behind the famous vertical CHICAGO sign. Tours offered.

sites.name: Route 66 Begin sign
sites.desc: The start of the Mother Road on Adams Street at Michigan Avenue.

sites.name: Lou Mitchell's
sites.desc: A diner since 1923 near the start of Route 66, known for handing out doughnut holes and Milk Duds.

sites.name: American Writers Museum
sites.desc: A museum devoted to American writers and their works, on Michigan Avenue.

sites.name: Chicago Riverwalk
sites.desc: A walkway along the main branch of the river, best paired with an architecture boat tour.

sites.name: Poetry Foundation
sites.desc: John Ronan's 2011 building with a screened garden and a free poetry library.

sites.name: Chicago Architecture Center and river cruise
sites.desc: Exhibitions on the city's buildings and the departure point of the docent-led architecture river cruises.

sites.name: Wrigley Building and Tribune Tower
sites.desc: Two 1920s towers framing the Michigan Avenue bridge: the white terra cotta Wrigley Building and the Gothic Tribune Tower.

sites.name: Marina City
sites.desc: Bertrand Goldberg's 1964 corncob towers, a city within a city on the river.

sites.name: Aqua Tower
sites.desc: Jeanne Gang's 2009 tower with undulating balconies that make the facade ripple like water.

sites.name: Lake Point Tower
sites.desc: A 1968 curving glass tower by students of Mies, inspired by his 1922 glass skyscraper project.

sites.name: Navy Pier
sites.desc: A 1916 municipal pier turned lakefront promenade with the Centennial Wheel and boat tours.

sites.name: 360 Chicago (John Hancock Center)
sites.desc: SOM's tapering, X-braced 1969 tower, with an observation deck on the 94th floor.

sites.name: Chicago Water Tower
sites.desc: The 1869 castellated limestone tower that survived the Great Fire of 1871.

sites.name: Fourth Presbyterian Church
sites.desc: Ralph Adams Cram's 1914 Gothic Revival church and cloister on Michigan Avenue.

sites.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago
sites.desc: One of the largest contemporary art museums in the country.

sites.name: Driehaus Museum
sites.desc: The restored 1883 Nickerson mansion, a showcase of Gilded Age interiors.

sites.name: Newberry Library
sites.desc: An independent research library with free exhibitions on maps, the Americas and the Midwest.

sites.name: Museum of Broadcast Communications
sites.desc: Radio and television history, including Chicago's role in early broadcasting.

sites.name: Merchandise Mart
sites.desc: The 1930 Art Deco giant on the river, with Art on theMART projections on its facade at night.

sites.name: Intuit: The Center for Intuitive and Outsider Art
sites.desc: Outsider and self-taught art, including Henry Darger's room.

sites.name: Field Museum
sites.desc: Natural history museum home to SUE, among the most complete T. rex skeletons found.

sites.name: Shedd Aquarium
sites.desc: A 1930 Beaux-Arts aquarium with an oceanarium overlooking the lake.

sites.name: Adler Planetarium
sites.desc: America's first planetarium (1930), with a classic skyline view from its peninsula.

sites.name: Soldier Field
sites.desc: The 1924 colonnaded stadium with a modern bowl inserted in 2003.

sites.name: Northerly Island
sites.desc: A former airport runway turned lakefront park with prairie, a lagoon and trails.

sites.name: Pritzker Military Museum and Library
sites.desc: Library and exhibitions on the citizen soldier, on Michigan Avenue.

sites.name: Museum of Contemporary Photography
sites.desc: A free photography museum at Columbia College Chicago.

sites.name: Buddy Guy's Legends
sites.desc: Blues club owned by Buddy Guy, with live music every night.

sites.name: Glessner House
sites.desc: H. H. Richardson's fortress-like 1887 house on Prairie Avenue, with an Arts and Crafts interior.

sites.name: Willie Dixon's Blues Heaven (Chess Records)
sites.desc: The former Chess studio at 2120 South Michigan, where Muddy Waters, Chuck Berry and Howlin' Wolf recorded.

sites.name: National Museum of Mexican Art
sites.desc: A free museum of Mexican art from antiquity to now, with a celebrated Day of the Dead exhibition each fall.

sites.name: Chinatown and Ping Tom Park
sites.desc: Wentworth Avenue's restaurants and shops and Ping Tom Memorial Park on the river.

sites.name: Chinese American Museum of Chicago
sites.desc: Museum of Chinese American history in the Midwest, in Chinatown.

sites.name: Union Station
sites.desc: Graham, Anderson, Probst and White's 1925 station with its vaulted Great Hall, where the Amtrak from Champaign arrives.

sites.name: Jane Addams Hull-House Museum
sites.desc: The settlement house founded by Jane Addams and Ellen Gates Starr in 1889, on the UIC campus. Free.

sites.name: National Hellenic Museum
sites.desc: Greek American history and culture in Greektown.

sites.name: Pilsen murals on 18th Street
sites.desc: A long tradition of Mexican and Chicano murals along 18th Street and the 16th Street rail embankment.

sites.name: Crown Hall, IIT
sites.desc: Mies van der Rohe's 1956 clear-span glass pavilion for the architecture school on his IIT campus.

sites.name: Union Stock Yard Gate
sites.desc: The 1879 limestone gate, the last remnant of the stockyards that fed the nation.

sites.name: Museum of Science and Industry
sites.desc: In the Palace of Fine Arts, the main surviving building of the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition.

sites.name: Robie House
sites.desc: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1910 Prairie masterpiece, part of the UNESCO listing of his work.

sites.name: Rockefeller Chapel
sites.desc: Bertram Goodhue's 1928 Gothic chapel at the University of Chicago, with a carillon.

sites.name: ISAC Museum
sites.desc: The University of Chicago's free museum of the ancient Middle East, formerly the Oriental Institute, with a colossal Assyrian lamassu.
sites.wiki: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures

sites.name: Smart Museum of Art
sites.desc: The University of Chicago's free art museum.

sites.name: DuSable Black History Museum
sites.desc: Founded in 1961 by Margaret Burroughs and others, one of the oldest museums of African American history.

sites.name: Obama Presidential Center
sites.desc: Tod Williams Billie Tsien's presidential center in Jackson Park. Check opening status and timed tickets.

sites.name: Garden of the Phoenix, Jackson Park
sites.desc: A Japanese garden on the Wooded Island of Olmsted's Jackson Park.

sites.name: Promontory Point
sites.desc: Alfred Caldwell's limestone-stepped lakefront peninsula with skyline views.

sites.name: South Shore Cultural Center
sites.desc: A 1916 Mediterranean Revival country club turned public park and arts center.

sites.name: Pullman National Historical Park
sites.desc: George Pullman's company town, site of the 1894 strike and later the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters.

sites.name: Big Marsh Park
sites.desc: A restored wetland and bike park on the far Southeast Side.

sites.name: Charnley-Persky House
sites.desc: An 1892 Gold Coast house by Louis Sullivan with the young Frank Lloyd Wright, home of the Society of Architectural Historians.

sites.name: Chicago History Museum
sites.desc: The city's history museum at the south end of Lincoln Park.

sites.name: Second City
sites.desc: The improv theater in Old Town that launched generations of comedians.

sites.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
sites.desc: A free zoo founded in 1868, with the Alfred Caldwell Lily Pool nearby.

sites.name: Lincoln Park Conservatory
sites.desc: A free Victorian glasshouse (1895) with palms, ferns and orchids.

sites.name: Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum
sites.desc: Nature museum in Lincoln Park with a butterfly haven.

sites.name: Wrightwood 659
sites.desc: Tadao Ando's interior inside a 1920s apartment building, an exhibition space with timed tickets.

sites.name: Biograph Theater
sites.desc: The Lincoln Avenue movie house where John Dillinger was shot in 1934, now a theater company's home.

sites.name: Kingston Mines
sites.desc: A long-running blues club with two stages in Lincoln Park.

sites.name: Wrigley Field
sites.desc: The Cubs' ivy-covered ballpark, opened in 1914.

sites.name: Music Box Theatre
sites.desc: A 1929 movie palace with a twinkling-star ceiling, still showing films daily.

sites.name: Graceland Cemetery
sites.desc: A landscape cemetery with tombs by Sullivan and the graves of Burnham, Mies and Sullivan.

sites.name: Montrose Point Bird Sanctuary
sites.desc: A lakefront habitat known as one of the best migration hotspots in the Midwest.

sites.name: Green Mill
sites.desc: Uptown jazz club operating since 1907, with live jazz nightly.

sites.name: Old Town School of Folk Music
sites.desc: A folk music school and concert venue in Lincoln Square since 1957.
sites.wiki: Old Town School of Folk Music

sites.name: Swedish American Museum
sites.desc: Museum of Swedish immigration in Andersonville.

sites.name: Superdawg Drive-In
sites.desc: A 1948 drive-in with two giant hot dog figures on its roof.

sites.name: Garfield Park Conservatory
sites.desc: Jens Jensen's 1908 glasshouse, designed as landscape art under glass. Free.

sites.name: The 606 (Bloomingdale Trail)
sites.desc: A 2.7 mile elevated rail trail through Wicker Park, Bucktown, Logan Square and Humboldt Park.

sites.name: Humboldt Park
sites.desc: Jens Jensen's prairie-style park with a lagoon and the historic boathouse.

sites.name: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts and Culture
sites.desc: In Humboldt Park's historic stables, a museum devoted to Puerto Rican arts and culture.
sites.wiki: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts and Culture

sites.name: Polish Museum of America
sites.desc: Founded in 1935, one of the oldest ethnic museums in the country.

sites.name: Holy Trinity Orthodox Cathedral
sites.desc: Louis Sullivan's 1903 Russian Orthodox cathedral in Ukrainian Village.

sites.name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
sites.desc: Wright's Oak Park home and studio from 1889 to 1909, where the Prairie style took shape.
sites.wiki: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio

sites.name: Unity Temple
sites.desc: Wright's 1908 concrete church in Oak Park, part of the UNESCO listing of his work.

sites.name: Ernest Hemingway Birthplace
sites.desc: The Oak Park Queen Anne house where Hemingway was born in 1899.

sites.name: Pleasant Home
sites.desc: George Maher's 1897 Prairie School mansion in Oak Park.

sites.name: Riverside
sites.desc: Olmsted and Vaux's 1869 planned suburb with curving streets.

sites.name: Brookfield Zoo
sites.desc: A large zoo that pioneered barless exhibits.

sites.name: Elmhurst Art Museum and McCormick House
sites.desc: Contemporary art museum built around Mies van der Rohe's McCormick House.

sites.name: Cantigny Park
sites.desc: Robert McCormick's estate in Wheaton, with the First Division Museum and gardens.

sites.name: Morton Arboretum
sites.desc: A 1,700 acre tree museum in Lisle with woodland trails and prairie.

sites.name: Fermilab
sites.desc: The particle physics lab in Batavia, with Wilson Hall, a prairie and a bison herd.

sites.name: Naper Settlement
sites.desc: An outdoor history museum of 19th-century buildings in Naperville.

sites.name: Illinois Holocaust Museum
sites.desc: Stanley Tigerman's museum in Skokie, founded by survivors.
sites.wiki: Illinois Holocaust Museum and Education Center

sites.name: Block Museum of Art
sites.desc: Northwestern University's free art museum in Evanston.
sites.wiki: Mary and Leigh Block Museum of Art

sites.name: Grosse Point Lighthouse
sites.desc: An 1873 lighthouse in Evanston, with a lakefront park.

sites.name: Bahá'í House of Worship
sites.desc: Louis Bourgeois's lace-like concrete temple in Wilmette, dedicated in 1953.

sites.name: Chicago Botanic Garden
sites.desc: Gardens on islands in Glencoe, with a Japanese garden and native prairie.

guides.title: Loop
guides.intro: Walk the Chicago School: the Rookery, Monadnock, Marquette and Reliance buildings, then the Art Institute and Millennium Park. A river cruise from the Architecture Center ties it together.

guides.title: Near North & River
guides.intro: The river and Michigan Avenue: the Wrigley and Tribune towers, Marina City and Aqua, the Water Tower and the MCA, with the Newberry and Driehaus a few blocks west.

guides.title: Museum Campus & South Loop
guides.intro: A full day on the lakefront peninsula with the Field, Shedd and Adler, then Prairie Avenue's Glessner House, Chess Records and dinner in Chinatown.

guides.title: Near West & Pilsen
guides.intro: Union Station, Hull-House and Greektown, then Pilsen's murals and the National Museum of Mexican Art, and Mies's IIT campus to the south.

guides.title: Hyde Park & South Side
guides.intro: Robie House, Rockefeller Chapel and the university museums, the Museum of Science and Industry, Jackson Park's Japanese garden and the DuSable. Pullman is a short Metra ride south.

guides.title: North Side & Lakefront
guides.intro: Lincoln Park's zoo and conservatory, the Chicago History Museum, Wrigley Field, Graceland Cemetery and an evening of jazz at the Green Mill.

guides.title: West Side
guides.intro: The Garfield Park Conservatory, The 606 trail, Humboldt Park and its Puerto Rican museum, and Sullivan's Holy Trinity Cathedral.

guides.title: Suburbs
guides.intro: Oak Park for Wright and Hemingway, Evanston and the Bahá'í Temple on the North Shore, and gardens and arboretums farther out.
